TECNALIA and AUTIS automate paint-inspection masks with AI

Development used more than 650 images spanning 20 vehicle models and 13 production lines to assess automated setup across factory environments.

TECNALIA ↗7 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Automating inspection-region setup

TECNALIA and AUTIS reported progress on AI-generated inspection masks for detecting paint defects on vehicle bodies. Specialists traditionally define these image regions manually for each vehicle model and installation. The work targets setup effort when commissioning visual-inspection systems; it does not introduce a painting robot or a new camera product.

A varied development dataset

Segmentation models generate masks from images captured by inspection systems. Development involved more than 650 images from six manufacturers, 20 vehicle models, eight plants and 13 production lines. This diversity supported evaluation across different industrial settings. The number of plants represented in the data is not a count of newly installed commercial products.

Feasibility without a quantified benchmark

TECNALIA says the results demonstrate technical feasibility and reduce configuration effort. The team also identified consistent labeling criteria as important for improving generalization. The announcement does not provide accuracy percentages, measured time savings or a separate test-set breakdown. Factories therefore need application-specific evaluation before drawing conclusions about their own returns.
